To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can: (1) create a unified sense inventory for knowledge base unification; (2) use this inventory to create a vector representation for relation argument pairs, which can be used for disambiguation and ranking; and (3) use this representation to align and merge different knowledge bases.

(1) sense-based embeddings of relation argument pairs can be used to improve the accuracy of relation argument disambiguation; (2) a large unified sense resource can be used to disambiguate the arguments of relations extracted from multiple heterogeneous knowledge bases; (3) a sense-based vector representation can be used to rank relations extracted from different knowledge bases by the degree of specificity of their domains and ranges. 1 http://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/ activities/KB-UNIFY

(1) sense embeddings can disambiguate Open Information Extraction outputs, (2) semantic similarity between domains and ranges can be used to align relations from different sources, and (3) the resulting unified knowledge base can be used as a starting point for further knowledge integration tasks.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of multiple knowledge bases can be done with high accuracy, and that the integration process is more effective when performed on a unified knowledge base.

, despite the heterogeneity and incompleteness of the knowledge extracted from different sources, we are now able to produce a unified knowledge base that is more comprehensive and accurate than any single source.
